programme: MEIS1, NPAS1 and HMX1 converge on the hypoxia-inducible transcription/catecholamine-synthesis axis: MEIS1 targets HIF1A directly, NPAS1 (a bHLH-PAS family member) targets its own obligate dimerization partners ARNT and ARNT2 plus the hypoxia-response effector EPO and the catecholamine-synthesis enzyme TH, and HMX1 independently converges on TH. Together these three factors wire onto the same small node set — HIF1A/ARNT/ARNT2 upstream, EPO and TH downstream — rather than being an incidental overlap.
role_in_a: In Pheochromocytoma_and_Paraganglioma this is the molecular logic of the 'pseudohypoxic' tumor subtype: stabilized HIF signaling drives ARNT-dependent transcription and excess catecholamine biosynthesis via TH, the defining secretory and metabolic phenotype of these chromaffin-lineage tumors. MEIS1->HIF1A and NPAS1->ARNT/ARNT2/TH would sit inside that wiring; HMX1's convergence on TH is also consistent with its known role in specifying the sympathetic/sensory neural-crest lineage chromaffin cells derive from.
role_in_b: In Stroke this is the acute hypoxic-response arm: ischemia stabilizes HIF1A, which signals through ARNT to induce protective genes, EPO among them, as an adaptive response to tissue hypoxia. NPAS1's targeting of ARNT/ARNT2 and EPO sits directly on that pathway.
shared_axis: Both diseases activate the same HIF/ARNT-centered transcriptional machinery, but for opposite reasons — constitutively and oncogenically in pseudohypoxic PCC/PGL, acutely and adaptively after ischemic injury in stroke — so factors that wire onto HIF1A, ARNT/ARNT2, EPO and TH would recur as concordant regulators in both settings even without disease crosstalk between them.
reasoning: Pseudohypoxic signaling in PCC/PGL and HIF/EPO-driven hypoxic response in stroke are each independently well established in their own disease literatures, so a shared hypoxia-axis explanation is biologically plausible without requiring a paper that states the pairing directly. But the retrieved record does not place MEIS1, NPAS1 or HMX1 in either disease — the reader's notes mark their papers as off-topic (sleep/leukemia, autism, neuronal subtypes respectively), Open Targets shows no PCC/PGL association for any of the three, and only a modest 0.29 percentile for MEIS1 in Stroke — so the account rests on the target-list convergence (HIF1A/ARNT/ARNT2/EPO/TH) and general pathway knowledge, not on retrieved evidence for the carrying factors themselves.
support: PMID 20534969 places ETV1 (not a carrying factor here) in malignant pheochromocytoma via epigenomic analysis; PMID 41989510 places MECP2 (not a carrying factor) in ischemic stroke via miR-132/Mecp2-mediated neuronal apoptosis; PMID 40602592 places ZFHX3 (not a carrying factor) in ischemic stroke via pericyte contraction/calcium influx. None of these concern MEIS1, NPAS1 or HMX1 — for the core hypoxia/catecholamine module itself, none found.
how_to_falsify: Run ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for MEIS1, NPAS1 and HMX1 in chromaffin/PCC tumor cells and in post-ischemic brain or cerebrovascular tissue to test whether they actually occupy the HIF1A, ARNT, ARNT2, EPO and TH loci in vivo — ReMap currently confirms only 1 of MEIS1's 15 listed targets and none of the others, so most of these links are predicted, not observed. If binding is absent, or if knocking down these factors does not shift HIF1A/ARNT/EPO/TH expression or catecholamine output in PCC/PGL models and does not shift EPO induction or infarct outcome in ischemia models, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Adrenal and blood are genuinely different tissues, and hypoxia/HIF signaling is a pathway shared across nearly all tissues, so convergence on it is a weaker signal of specific crosstalk than a tissue-restricted module would be. Support is drawn from 30 patient-group comparisons across only 4 independent cohort pairs, and the three carrying factors sit mid-table (18/30, 16/30, 16/30), not near-universal. Most listed MEIS1/TEAD2/ETV1/THAP1 target bindings are ReMap-unconfirmed, so target lists are largely predicted. The single-view exclusions (TSHZ1, MSC, etc.) show no hidden hypoxia-pathway signal was dropped for being cohort-specific, and the tissue-generic exclusions (FOS, JUNB, STAT5A, IRF1, etc. — classic immediate-early/stress-response factors) were correctly removed rather than being the true driver. MECP2 and ZFHX3 do have direct stroke-specific papers, but through mechanisms (neuronal apoptosis, pericyte calcium handling) unconnected to the HIF/catecholamine module, so this account covers only a subset of the recurring factors, not all twelve.
